dedupe_keys.name: wuhan qingshan sponge city stormwater regulation effectiveness with swmm frontiers in water 2024

description: This case study is a Frontiers in Water paper of October 2024 that evaluates how well Wuhan's sponge city construction regulates stormwater in the South Trunk Canal area of the Qingshan Demonstration Area. The authors build a Storm Water Management Model, SWMM, of the drainage network and simulate runoff and pipe drainage capacity before and after sponge construction in typical high, normal and low flow years and for different return periods. The results show sponge construction significantly regulates annual runoff and reduces overflow at 1- and 5-year return periods, but against short-duration storms it is effective only at the 1-year return period, and its effect fades as flood size grows; the discussion proposes the National Water Network Project to connect water systems and cover these gaps. Coverage: one demonstration area, simulated scenarios. Access: free article; the article is CC BY; model files and data availability were not read beyond the abstract. Caveats: SWMM results depend on calibration that was not reviewed here. It informs stormwater retrofit and low impact development design checks, and relates to EPA SWMM and the Guangxi sponge city case study in the catalogue.
